questions.q: Which three forces does Friedman say we must understand to make sense of our times?
a: Technology, globalization and climate change
Politics, religion and education
Population, trade and energy
Media, migration and finance
questions.why: The overview names these three forces, all accelerating at once and reshaping every part of life.

questions.q: How is technology changing dairy farming, according to the summary?
a: Computers now monitor milk flow and supply chains
Robots have removed the need for any milking
Farmers sell their milk directly to consumers online
Cows are bred to produce smaller quantities of milk
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes farmers becoming data analysts as computers track udders, milk flow and supplies.

questions.q: What did the 2013 Oxford study find about American jobs?
a: Nearly half were at high risk of being automated
Most new jobs required a college degree
Wages had risen fastest in farming work
Remote work would soon replace office jobs
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites the study’s figure that 47 percent of jobs could be lost to computers within 20 years.

questions.q: What does the ASOS dress example show about today’s globalized market?
a: A single photo can make a product sell out instantly
Celebrities design most of the clothes people buy
Online stores struggle to keep up with demand
Fashion trends now fade more slowly than before
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses the 816,000 retweets of Michelle Obama’s dress to show how fast products can go viral.

questions.q: Why is Friedman optimistic about our ability to handle climate change?
a: Technology and globalization let people collaborate worldwide
Governments have already met their climate targets
Populations are shrinking, so emissions will fall
New resources have been found to replace the old ones
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that shared internet access lets humanity work together on common problems.
